absent: Behavior of the shared fast insertion path including duplicate detection and table growth.
Bucket table layout, hash computation, bucket selection, and locking primitives.
Resize, rehash, walk, free, shrink threshold, and deferred work protocols.
Core bitmap allocation, clearing reconciliation, swap locking, and wait plus wakeup protocols.
Scatter table allocation, mapping, DMA semantics, and segmented construction limits.

findings.text: List table insertion is offered with an explicit key and with a key derived from the queued member using the configured displacement, both delegating to the shared fast insertion path and returning its failure encoding as a negative status.

Insertion for members carrying their own key has a status form and a pointer form; the status form reports success on absence and a conflict on presence, while the pointer form returns the conflicting member directly.

Insertion with a caller supplied key has a status form and a pointer form with the same success versus conflict contract as the embedded key forms, but it is intended for tables using an external hash callback.

Removal is offered for plain members and for list members through one shared helper that retries across successive table generations linked as future versions and reports not found when no generation contains the target.

Replacement exchanges an old member for a new member found by the same hash and retries across future table generations like removal, failing without mutation when the old member is absent or hashes differ.
List table walk entry and teardown delegate to the underlying table walk and free plus destroy helpers, with plain destroy supplying empty reclamation arguments.
When the key is embedded, its address is the member object base advanced by the table or parameter key displacement; explicit key forms use the caller address unchanged.
Embedded key insertion requires that no object hash callback be configured, while explicit key insertion requires such a callback plus a present key; violations invoke the platform bug check.
Status insertion forms map a fast path error encoding to a negative status, a null outcome to success, and any other returned pointer to an existence conflict.

Single table removal distinguishes missing entries from detached queued members and detached chain heads, with only head detachment adjusting the global element count before all outcomes collapse to success or not found.
Replacement requires equal hash values for old and new members as a proxy for identifier equality and rejects mismatched pairs as invalid without accessing any bucket.
Successful head detachment decrements the global count and, when automatic shrinking is enabled and occupancy is below a low threshold, schedules deferred table work.
Single table removal and replacement hold one bucket lock while scanning and updating links, using an assign plus unlock path when the bucket head slot changes and a plain unlock path otherwise.

Multi table removal and replacement run inside a read side critical section while following the current table and then any future tables, relying on prior bucket locking in the older table to make a not yet visible newer table conclusive.
Scalable bitmap word unit contains an allocation word and a deferred release word on a separate cache line plus a raw spin lock serializing joint updates; the whole unit is cache line aligned.
Scalable bitmap descriptor records total depth, log width per word, word count, round robin policy, pointer to the word array, and a per processor hint caching a recent position.
Bitmap queue descriptor embeds a bitmap and adds a wake batch threshold, a wake index, a wait queue array, an active queue count, a minimum shallow depth, and completion plus wakeup counters.
Wait state holds one wait queue head and is cache line aligned; the waiter object pairs a queue pointer used for accounting with a wait queue entry.

A global bit number splits into a word index by shifting with the configured width and an offset within the word by masking; every word except the last is full width while the last covers only the remaining depth.
Per word usable width is selected from machine word size and then reduced for small depths so that tiny bitmaps still spread across several cache lines, with depths below four left at full width.
Bitmap iteration visits allocated bits that are not deferred cleared, starting from a caller position with wrap to the start and stopping early when the callback declines to continue.

Direct bit manipulation sets, clears, tests, and deferred clears individual positions through the word array; release marks deferred state and refreshes the processor hint unless round robin or an invalid position applies.

Allocated state and deferred release state live in distinct words so that release does not immediately disturb concurrent allocation scans; teardown releases the per processor hints and the word array and clears the map pointer.
Queue allocation pins the calling processor, records its identity for the caller, delegates to the core allocator, then unpins before returning the result.
Wait queue selection advances round robin modulo the fixed queue count, with an atomic compare exchange retry form for shared indices and a fetch plus advance helper returning the selected queue.
Scatter entry holds a tagged page link plus offset, length, device address, and optionally device length and device flags depending on build options.
Scatter table holds a list pointer plus mapped and original entry counts; the append variant adds the last populated entry and a total capacity.
The low two bits of the page link encode chain versus end markers, leaving the remaining bits for the page address; helpers expose the flags, extract a chain pointer, and test each marker.

Traversal returns no successor at an end marker and otherwise follows to the next entry, transparently jumping through chain links; table iteration macros bound such walks by original or mapped counts.

Chain construction clears offset and length in the link entry, sets the chain marker and clears the end marker; marking an end sets the end marker and clears chain, while unmarking clears only the end marker.

Page, folio, and buffer assignment preserve existing chain and end markers while installing the new page and geometry; accessors recover the page, physical address, and kernel virtual address from that stored state.
Device flag queries and updates either manipulate stored flag bits or behave as constant false plus no operation stubs, depending on whether the build retains device flags.
Table construction from a page array is a thin wrapper that forwards to a segmented constructor with an unlimited segment bound.
Allocation and release callbacks for scatter arrays are typed as a sized allocator returning a list and a sized release helper.
Queue wait structure count is eight and the default wake batch size is eight.
Page link chain marker is value one and end marker is value two, with their combination forming the mask of tag bits.
Device bus address flag is bit zero and bounce buffer flag is bit one of the device flag word.
Device address is read from the dedicated device address field; device length is either a dedicated device length field or the base length field depending on build options.

Maximum single allocation count is one page divided by one entry size, chunk size is one hundred twenty eight, and maximum segment count is either the chunk size or two thousand forty eight depending on build options.
A scatter slot is in exactly one of plain, end, or chain link states; chaining consumes the last slot of a segment as a link, while end marking designates list termination.

A bitmap position moves from free to allocated on set, to released pending on deferred mark, and back to free after a later reconciliation; scans observe only allocated positions that lack a pending release mark.

Page assignment requires page pointer alignment that leaves the tag bits clear and rejects chain entries under debug builds; folio geometry beyond unsigned range and non contiguous page ranges raise warnings.
Bitmap scans normalize an out of range start to zero and always advance through every word with wrap, so callers must bound work through the callback rather than relying on positional termination.

Removal and replacement treat a missing bucket as not found before locking; list aware removal splices around queued duplicates under the same bucket lock and preserves a successor queued member when the head itself is removed.
